caption:
🏙️ Central Tokyo, every building standing today by year of construction — 1920 → 2021.

Almost nothing from before 1945 survives: the 1923 earthquake and the 1945 firebombing destroyed most of the old city, and Tokyo rebuilds fast, a building rarely lasts more than 40 years. The red pockets are the post-war rebuild, then the high-growth years and the 1980s bubble, and finally the towers of the bay. Landmarks keep their real completion year.

📊 Data: footprints and measured heights from PLATEAU (MLIT, open data). Japan publishes no open building-age register: only the ~7% of buildings flagged as new since 2016 are measured, all other years are estimated from the history and housing statistics of each ward. Heights exaggerated.
🌍 Map: OpenStreetMap contributors; ward boundaries MLIT.
